title: HydroSheaf: a claim-gated evidence-integration framework for groundwater connectivity, residence-time and reaction inference in data-limited aquifers
scope: A software and methods research article for Computers & Geosciences. It documents the implemented HydroSheaf package, characterises the Ghanaian hydrochemical datasets it is applied to, and reports what each component of the framework can and cannot establish under controlled-synthetic tests, external reference comparisons and a real-data application.

objectives.statement: Describe the implemented software architecture and the evidence-to-claim pipeline that separates candidate generation, specialist scoring, calibration, discrepancy handling and claim gating.
acceptance_criteria: Every reported capability maps to a named package module
The PASS, WEAK and ABSTAIN decision states are defined operationally

objectives.statement: Characterise the three Ghanaian hydrochemical datasets so that a reader can judge what inference they support, including variable coverage, analytical quality and isotopic character.
acceptance_criteria: Charge-balance error is computed independently from the reported ions
Every absent variable that would be required for a stronger claim is listed
The reconstructed Northern Ghana seasonal attribute is stated explicitly

objectives.statement: Quantify component recovery under a 100-realisation synthetic benchmark with known truth, separating targets that are recoverable from targets that are not.
acceptance_criteria: Transport, residence-time and reaction-extent recovery are reported separately
A negative or null recovery result is reported rather than suppressed

objectives.statement: Report the locked controlled-synthetic programme gates for calibrated age, reaction-family, kinetic and integrated decision performance against predeclared thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Observed values are reported beside the thresholds fixed before scoring
Structural non-identifiability is reported as an abstention, not imputed

objectives.statement: Compare framework output against evidence generated outside the study: published lumped-parameter age estimates and a particle-tracking directed topology.
acceptance_criteria: Held-out uncalibrated agreement is the primary reported comparison
Calibrated emulation is labelled as emulation and never as agreement
Prior-assisted topology ingestion is never pooled with independent inference

objectives.statement: Apply the framework to the measured field datasets and report the resulting evidence ceiling.
acceptance_criteria: Candidate edges are described as screening constructions, not flow paths
In-sample closure is never described as predictive validation

inputs.provenance: Author-compiled regional panel; chemistry measured, seasonal separation reconstructed (DECISION D2)
100-realisation synthetic recovery benchmark and directed-topology comparison
Comparison against published lumped-parameter age outputs

risks.risk: A reconstructed data attribute is reported as a measurement.
risks.mitigation: The Northern Ghana seasonal panel is excluded from inference and its status is stated in the Data section, the limitations and the availability statement.

risks.risk: Calibrated emulation of a reference is read as independent agreement.
risks.mitigation: Held-out uncalibrated parity is the primary result; the calibrated result is labelled emulation wherever it appears.

risks.risk: In-sample chemistry closure is read as connectivity validation.
risks.mitigation: Candidate edges are described as coordinate-neighbour screening constructions throughout.

risks.risk: Values are inherited from an earlier manuscript rather than recomputed.
risks.mitigation: Every value is regenerated by scripts under M2.3/analysis/python; disagreements are recorded in evidence_discrepancies.csv.

risks.risk: The locked run was generated from an uncommitted working tree.
risks.mitigation: The provenance limitation is stated in Methods, the limitations and the reproducibility statement; a clean rerun is a declared submission action.
